headline: AI-generated women are stealing comedians' jokes for NSFW content
summary: Comedians are finding their jokes replicated verbatim by AI-generated influencers promoting OnlyFans-like platforms, raising concerns about content theft and creator protection.
details: Stand-up comedians are reporting that AI-generated social media personalities are stealing their jokes and performing them in sexually suggestive videos. Comedian Julia Jasunas discovered her joke being used by an AI influencer named Aylen Skye, whose content promotes NSFW subscription platforms.

Jasunas noted that the comments on AI-generated accounts are overwhelmingly positive and objectifying, unlike those on real comedians' posts, which often include criticism. She reported the video to Meta for impersonation, but the platform stated it did not violate guidelines as Skye wasn't impersonating Jasunas, only her joke.

WIRED has identified at least eight comedians whose content has been replicated by these AI influencers. These accounts often use better production quality, more revealing outfits, and sometimes even generate fake interviews with celebrities to increase virality.

The AI-generated content not only steals jokes but also sexualizes them, profiting off creators' work. Comedians like Mandy Martino are calling for better protections, emphasizing that this trend represents a significant shift in content creation and intellectual property rights.

The technology behind these AI clones is rapidly improving, making it increasingly difficult to distinguish them from real people. Accounts like Tiffany Sloane, which identifies as an actress, feature crowd work and jokes, also linking to adult content platforms.
caption:
AI influencers are stealing comedians' jokes and performing them in sexually explicit videos, raising alarms in the comedy community.

Stand-up comedians are reporting that AI-generated social media personalities are stealing their jokes and performing them in sexually suggestive videos. Comedian Julia Jasunas discovered her joke being used by an AI influencer named Aylen Skye, whose content promotes NSFW subscription platforms.

Jasunas noted that the comments on AI-generated accounts are overwhelmingly positive and objectifying, unlike those on real comedians' posts, which often include criticism. She reported the video to Meta for impersonation, but the platform stated it did not violate guidelines as Skye wasn't impersonating Jasunas, only her joke.

WIRED has identified at least eight comedians whose content has been replicated by these AI influencers. These accounts often use better production quality, more revealing outfits, and sometimes even generate fake interviews with celebrities to increase virality.

The AI-generated content not only steals jokes but also sexualizes them, profiting off creators' work. Comedians like Mandy Martino are calling for better protections, emphasizing that this trend represents a significant shift in content creation and intellectual property rights.

The technology behind these AI clones is rapidly improving, making it increasingly difficult to distinguish them from real people. Accounts like Tiffany Sloane, which identifies as an actress, feature crowd work and jokes, also linking to adult content platforms.
